intent: A dark, monochrome bulk invite that treats seats as the subject: pasted emails become rows with their own roles, invalid addresses stay flagged, and Send flies each avatar into a pending list while the seat meter fills.

stack.styling: Tailwind CSS v4 with @container queries; colour tokens as CSS variables on the root; color-mix() for preview pills and focus rings
stack.animation: motion/react: entrance blur, layoutId so avatars fly from the paste well into Pending, layoutId for the role-menu highlight, rolling seat and send counts
stack.fonts: font-sans (Geist) for UI, font-display (Geist) for the heading and seat count, font-mono (Geist Mono) for labels and the Guest tag

layout.card: surface, 1px line, 14px radius, inset highlight + deep shadow, no overflow hidden, @container root, 560px max in the demo
layout.header: 18px display title and mono workspace on the left; 32px tabular seat count with a mono ‘of 8’ on the right
layout.meter: 8px pills, 3px gap: ink taken, ghost preview, line empty, danger over-seat. 13px sentence under it
layout.team: five 24px overlapping initials and a truncated ‘5 on the team · first names’ line, removable with showTeam
layout.well: sunken, 12px radius. Rows then a 36px paste field. Valid row is avatar, name, Guest tag, email, role menu, remove. Invalid row is an alert icon, danger text, a 2px danger rail, and the reason instead of a role
layout.footer: hairline, PENDING count, dashed empty tray or pending rows with the flown avatar, ‘Invited · role · email’, and withdraw

typography.title: display 18px semibold, tracking -0.03em
typography.seats: display 32px semibold, tracking -0.04em, tabular, leading none
typography.name: 14px medium
typography.email: 12px faint, or danger when the row is flagged

color.approach: greyscale; one accent on the Send button and the selected role check; danger only for flagged addresses and seats past the plan
color.accent: theme ink by default. Button label is black or white from relative luminance

motion.order: card, header, meter, team, well, then seat pills scaling from the left 35ms apart
motion.counts: seat total and the Send count roll with a 3px blur
motion.paste: separators and paste split addresses into rows; blur commits; a ref stops Send’s blur from inserting twice
motion.send: valid avatars share a layoutId with their pending row and fly on a 380/34 spring; invalid rows stay
motion.menus: 6px offset, 0.98 scale, 4px blur; highlight on spring 500/40
motion.reducedMotion: 150ms fades only, no flight and no pill scale

responsive.320: avatar, full name and remove stay on one line; the role trigger drops under the email; Send is full width; the team line is just the count
responsive.390: same stack as 320. Names such as Kade Adeyemi stay whole, with the Guest tag beside them
responsive.768+: role trigger sits on the row’s right; Send sits on the hint’s right at a 9.5rem minimum width

accessibility: seat meter is role=img with a name that includes taken, included and how many the send would add
paste field is aria-invalid when any row is flagged and aria-describedby the hint
seat sentence and the pending list update in a polite live region
role menu is a listbox: arrows, Enter, Space, Escape, Tab, dismiss on outside pointer
remove and withdraw buttons name the address or person
avatars are aria-hidden; 2px focus-visible outlines in ink

content.product: Ledgerline’s website review, filling the last seats before Friday
content.team: Sam Okoye (owner), Mara Ilić, Jonas Weber, Priya Raman, Pablo Ferreira — 5 of 8
content.pasted: Inês Duarte (editor), Rafi Mendel (commenter), Kade Adeyemi (guest, viewer), the broken ‘priya@’, and sam@ledgerline.co who is already on the team
content.demo: types leah@ledgerline.co, who resolves to Leah Okon, then sends; the four valid people land in Pending and the meter reads 9 of 8

avoid: a share dialog with link access and a full member list
one role for the whole batch
dropping invalid emails instead of flagging them in place
blocking send when the invite goes past the included seats
closing the role menu on blur in a way that eats the option click
